text:
anais: quick follow-up from the postmortem — we keep seeing the same triad: quota bursts from nightly embedding backfills, scheduler churn during model rollouts, and transient KV cache misses. proposing a small ownership map + acceptance criteria so these don't keep coming back.

anais: proposed owners:
- lee: nightly job throttles + backfill coordination
- tomas: scheduler stabilization (preemption tuning + packer thresholds)
- elena: quota backstop + emergency override policy
- anais: acceptance tests + follow-through on closure

lee: ack. I'll add a gating job for embedding backfills that checks pool headroom before starting. Plan: add a preflight check and a soft window (02:00-04:00) and stagger shards.

lee: sample preflight check command I'm prototyping:
```
# check headroom before starting backfill
curl -s "https://infra-api.internal/headroom?window=30m" | jq '.available_gpu_pct' | awk '{ if ($1 < 25) exit 1 }'
```

anais: nice. Can you also emit an event to #incidents when the preflight blocks a run so ops knows?

lee: will do, tagging ops-bot to create an alert rule on event.

ops-bot: New ticket INF-3765 created: "Embedding backfill preflight + staggered window" assigned -> lee. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-3765 :robot_face:

elena: ack. On quota backstops I'll draft two profiles: (A) strict backstop for production customers and (B) lenient for research/experiments. Emergency override only via SRE pager with justification. Also adding notification cadence at 70% and hard throttle at 95%.

tomas: for scheduler churn my first target is the preemption aggressiveness and the age-based decayer for small jobs. I want to reduce unnecessary preemptions that cause spotty packing. Proposal: increase min_run_time to 30s and lower preemption_score_weight.

tomas: quick config diff I'll test in sandbox:
```
min_run_time_s: 30
preemption_score_weight: 0.6
packer_bin_target: 0.82
```

anais: add a canary plan please. small dedicated pool + internal traffic only. include rollback commands.

tomas: planning a 3-GPU canary pool named "sched-stable-canary". will run 48h soak with synthetic traffic.

ops-bot: New ticket INF-3766 created: "Scheduler decay + canary pool" assigned -> tomas. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-3766 :robot_face:

elena: two notes from the postmortem: 1) KV cache warming on rollouts reduces thrash — we should schedule a short warming window immediately after deploys, 2) quota telemetry needs higher cardinality to link spikes to customers.

anais: agreed on both. For KV warming let's add a short-run at 5% traffic that seeds hot keys. For telemetry, elena can you propose fields we need? customer_id, team, job_type, model_version, pool_id?

elena: exactly that + request_path and token_count. I'll add a PR to the metrics repo.

sre-oncall: runbook ask: add clear decision points for when to add capacity vs route to fallback model. Suggest: if predicted headroom < 15% for next 10m AND autoscale failed to provision within 120s -> start routing policy. I'll write the checklist.

anais: good. Let's lock acceptance criteria for closure on tickets:
- backfill ticket: blocking preflight in place + 2 successful staggered runs
- scheduler ticket: canary soak >=48h with <1% error rate and no new preempt spikes
- quota ticket: new backstop policy applied to prod + alerts at 70%/90% tested

lee: timeline request: can we aim to complete canaries and policy PRs within 10 working days? I'm constrained next week but can start infra this week.

tomas: reasonable. I'll aim to have sandbox tests by day 3 and canary ready by day 6.

elena: I can open the policy PR today and get security review in 4 business days.

ops-bot: Reminder: recurring task created -> "GPU-capacity followup check-in" every Wed 11:00 starting next week.

anais: ok owners, please add due dates in the Jira tickets and paste links here. I'll consolidate into a short weekly burndown doc and mark blockers. If anyone needs pairing time for the canaries ping me.

lee: adding note: we'll also throttle low-priority cron jobs automatically if headroom drops during run. Will post the throttle list.

elena: acked :white_check_mark: I'll include the emergency override playbook and a short train-the-trainer doc for SREs.

tomas: ack :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: I'll update the incident playbook with the new decision points and link the canary run instructions.

anais: thanks team — goal is to break the recurrence loop, not just patch symptoms. Closing thread, will post burndown status next Wed.
